verdict.rationale: iTerm2's AI features are documented as optional/opt-in (docs-15), implying user control over whether terminal data is sent to third-party AI providers like OpenAI, but hands-on community reports show this control was not reliable in practice — the OpenAI key field activated data-sending even with garbage/empty input, contradicting the expectation of a true opt-out (comm-2), and this fueled real backlash (comm-1, comm-3). There is no vendor documentation addressing model-training opt-out specifically, only the toggle to enable/disable the feature itself. Missing for 10: explicit privacy/training-opt-out policy documentation, confirmation the bug was fixed, and independent verification that no data reaches OpenAI when disabled.
